candidates.api_shape: rotary_hook(hook_r, bobbin_d, phase_deg) -> {hook, bobbin_case} 2:1 with the needle
candidates.fdm: A spinning hook and a stationary bobbin case. Prints. The Singer lock-stitch cell. Phase is hook angle; needle timing is 2:1 asserted, not invented from contact.
candidates.name: rotary_hook
candidates.why: The stitch primitive. Needle leaves a loop, hook carries it around the bobbin. Not a cam and not a slider-crank. Every printed sewing demo invents this from a cylinder.

candidates.api_shape: a boat shuttle that rocks through ~180 deg around a bobbin, 507 #397
candidates.fdm: A pointed boat + a race. Prints. Howe-style. Older, slower, very printable.
candidates.name: oscillating_shuttle
candidates.why: The other lock-stitch cell. 507's named shuttle motion. Distinct from rotary_hook (continuous spin vs rock).

candidates.api_shape: heddle(eye_w, wire_t, frame) -> an eye on a lift frame, n of them on a harness
candidates.fdm: A thin frame with an eye. Prints flat. The warp-lift cell. A harness is n heddles; a loom is a product.
candidates.name: heddle
candidates.why: Weaving shed. Every warp thread through an eye. Not a needle and not a reed. The missing loom primitive.

candidates.api_shape: reed(dents, width, height) -> a comb that beats weft
candidates.fdm: A comb of printed dents. Prints. Beat-up cell.
candidates.name: reed
candidates.why: The other weaving cell. Heddles shed, the reed beats. A comb, not a gear.

candidates.api_shape: an eyed lever driven by a heart or plate cam, or a four-bar
candidates.fdm: A lever with an eye. heart_cam's usecase already names this. A thin named kit on that cam.
candidates.name: take_up_lever
candidates.why: Pulls slack after the hook. The motion is a cam; the part is an eyed lever. Do not add a second cam.

candidates.api_shape: a guided bar plus a needle, driven by a crank or a cam
candidates.name: needle_bar
candidates.why: The needle's prismatic. Agents invent it from cyl. A named bar on slider_crank / linear_way, not a new pair.

candidates.api_shape: a hook that a knife may or may not catch, selected by a card or a pin
candidates.fdm: A hook + a knife. Prints. The selector cell. The card reader is a product.
candidates.name: jacquard_hook
candidates.why: Jacquard 1804. Binary lift of one warp. Distinct from a heddle (always on a harness) and from a detent.

candidates.api_shape: toothed plate with a 4-motion (up, forward, down, back)
candidates.fdm: Prints. The 4-motion is two cams or a spatial link. Getting product-shaped.
candidates.name: feed_dog
candidates.why: Fabric feed. Real, but the law is two cams. After rotary_hook exists.

candidates.name: sewing_machine_product
candidates.why: Bed, arm, motor, tensioners. Product. The cells are hook + take-up + needle bar.

candidates.name: loom_product
candidates.why: Frame, warp beam, cloth beam. Product.

rejected.name: rapier_loom
rejected.why: A pick system that is a finished loom. The reusable part is a rod + gripper, close to a product.

rejected.name: overlock_looper
rejected.why: Serger loopers are a product stitch type. After lock-stitch exists.

sources: mechlib/usecases.py heart_cam sewing take-up, barrel_cam textile traverse, mechlib/cams.py, mechlib/linkages.py slider_crank
summary:
Textile machines make a stitch or a shed. Lock-stitch (Howe 1846, Singer rotary hook later) is needle + hook/shuttle + take-up: the needle leaves a loop, the hook carries it around a bobbin, the take-up sets the knot. Weaving is shed (heddles lift warp), pick (shuttle or rapier carries weft), beat-up (reed). Jacquard is a hook that chooses which warp lifts. 507 names shuttle motion 397, warp-dressing 383, spinning throstle 496. Heart-cam's usecase already mentions sewing-machine take-up; barrel_cam mentions textile traverse. No other textile API exists.

Catalog has the motion neighbours, not the textile cells. slider_crank / watt_six (proposed) can drive a needle bar. heart_cam and plate_cam can time take-up. geneva and cams can index a feed. iris is not a reed. Grep finds no rotary hook, bobbin case, needle bar, heddle, reed, rapier, or Jacquard hook.

FDM reality. rotary_hook is a 2:1 spinning hook around a stationary bobbin case; prints as two pieces, the Singer cell, and it is the missing stitch primitive. Oscillating shuttle is the older Howe cell (a boat that rocks). take_up_lever is a cam-driven or four-bar eye that pulls slack; heart_cam already claims the job, so a named lever on that cam is enough. needle_bar is a guided prismatic plus a needle; composition of linear_way + a bar. heddle is an eye in a frame, the warp-lift cell. reed is a comb that beats weft. Jacquard hook is a lifted hook that catches a knife; the card/computer is a product. A sewing machine or a loom is a finished product. Rapier and projectile looms are products built on a pick cell.
title: Sewing, weaving, and textile mechanisms
